name: BQ24005PWPR
title: Two-cell Li-ion linear charge management IC (bq24004, bq24005, bq24006)
summary: The bq24004, bq24005 and bq24006 are linear chargers for 2-cell lithium-ion batteries, with the P-channel pass FET, a reverse-blocking Schottky and thermal shutdown on the chip. They charge in three phases: a low-current precondition for deeply discharged cells, constant current set by an external sense resistor (up to 1.2 A), then constant voltage at 8.2 V or 8.4 V chosen by a pin, held within ±1 %. Charge stops on a minimum-current (taper) timer or on a selectable 3, 4.5 or 6 h safety timer, and a thermistor or adapter-voltage input can gate it. The three parts differ in their status outputs: one LED, two LEDs (open drain) or one bicolour LED.

circuits.title: Li-ion / Li-polymer charger
circuits.description: A complete two-cell charger built round a bq24005. The adapter's DC+ is the VCC rail, held up by C1; a 0.1 Ω sense resistor R1 feeds both IN pins and ISNS, which sets roughly 1 A of fast-charge current (0.1 V / 0.1 Ω). VCC, EN and VSEL all sit on the rail, so the charger is always enabled and regulates at 8.4 V. C2 decouples VCC and C3 holds up the CR regulator. R2 from CR and R3 to ground form the thermistor divider; the pack's thermistor, between PACK- and TEMP, lies in parallel with R3 at APG/THERM. OUT drives PACK+, VSENSE senses PACK+, C4 sits across the pack terminals, and AGND returns to PACK-. Two LEDs with 500 Ω resistors to VCC hang on the open-drain STAT1 and STAT2 outputs. TMR SEL is open, which selects the 3 h timer.
notes: With TMR SEL left open (3 h timer), a 10 pF capacitor goes from TMR SEL to CR.

A host reading the STAT pins may need hysteresis added in its feedback to stop them toggling while the current crosses the taper-detect threshold, usually for under half a second. The SLUU083 and SLUU113 EVMs show added STAT resistors.

circuits.title: Temperature sensing
circuits.description: Partial circuit: the thermistor input alone. CR, bypassed by C3, biases a divider of RT1 to APG/THERM and RT2 to ground; the NTC thermistor inside the pack runs from PACK- to TEMP, and TEMP joins APG/THERM. RT1 and RT2 come from the RT1/RT2 equations for the chosen hot and cold trip temperatures.

circuits.title: APG sensing
circuits.description: Partial circuit: adapter-power-good input alone. R1 and R2 divide the VCC supply (DC+) down to APG/THERM, so charging is allowed only while the divided adapter voltage lies inside the APG/THERM window. R2 returns to DC-, which is ground.

circuits.title: Current sensing
circuits.description: Partial circuit: the input side. DC+ is the VCC rail, with C1 as the bulk capacitor; R(SNS) carries the charge current from VCC to both IN pins and ISNS, and its value is V(ilim) / I(REG). VCC and EN connect to the rail, with C2 decoupling it.

operation.text: A cycle runs precondition, then constant current at I(lim), then constant voltage at the selected regulation voltage until termination. Preconditioning and the post-taper stage each last 22.5 minutes at most; the overall charge timer (3, 4.5 or 6 h) covers the current and voltage phases.

A cycle starts once power is applied with a battery connected, and only while the APG/THERM input is in range. Below the LowV threshold (5.75 V typ) the fast-charge path is held off and a separate precharge source supplies about 60 mA, which also keeps dissipation in the pass FET low. A 22.5-minute timer bounds precharge; if the cell has not risen above LowV when it expires, the IC flags a fault.

APG/THERM is watched continuously against two internal thresholds, V(TP1) (upper, 1.498 V typ) and V(TP2) (lower, 0.558 V typ). Between them charging proceeds; above or below, charging is suspended as a fault. A divider from CR with an NTC or PTC thermistor turns pack temperature into this voltage, or a divider from VCC turns adapter voltage into it. Falling edges are deglitched over 25 µs to 75 µs.

While the pack is below the regulation voltage, the loop holds the drop across the sense resistor, measured between VCC and ISNS, at V(ilim), 0.1 V typ. The resistor sits between the supply and the IN pins; 0.083 Ω to 1 Ω covers 100 mA to 1.2 A.

VSENSE carries the battery voltage feedback and connects straight to the pack's positive terminal, routed to the cells' own terminals for best accuracy. VSEL low gives 8.2 V (coke anode cells), VSEL high 8.4 V (graphite anode cells). A 10 kΩ resistor inside connects VSENSE to OUT.

Charge ends on the first of two events. The safety timer, chosen on TMR SEL, starts after preconditioning and restarts with each new cycle. In the voltage phase, once the current drops under the taper threshold (18.5 mV typ across the sense resistor, about a fifth of V(ilim)) a 22.5-minute timer runs and fast charge ends when it expires. The timer is held, not reset, during a fault (APG/THERM out of its window, or thermal shutdown). When the safety timer runs out, the charger switches off and shows DONE.

A VSENSE voltage above the OverV threshold (9.00 V typ) during precharge or fast charge moves the charger into its fault state. If the battery falls below LowV during fast charge, the cycle returns to qualification.

After DONE, a new cycle starts when the battery falls below the HighV recharge threshold (7.85 V typ), on a power-on reset, or when APG/THERM or EN toggles. A fault clears on a power-on reset or a toggle of APG/THERM or EN.

bq24004 drives one LED from STAT1, bq24005 two separate LEDs from STAT1 and STAT2, bq24006 one bicolour LED from both. bq24004 and bq24006 have totem-pole outputs; bq24005's are open drain. STAT1 and STAT2 are rated to 10 mA sink or source (absolute maximum).

The on-chip pass transistor is a P-channel MOSFET with a reverse-blocking Schottky, so no current flows from OUT back to IN. Above about 165 °C junction temperature the FET turns off; it turns on again after the die cools by about 10 °C, cycling while the fault lasts.
EN high runs the charger; EN low shuts it down into a standby mode drawing about 1 µA from VCC. EN has a 100 kΩ to 200 kΩ pulldown inside.
The IC starts when VCC rises past 8.9 V typ and stops below 8.66 V typ. A power-on delay of 1.2 ms to 3 ms follows start-up.

The PWP package is a 20-pin TSSOP with an exposed thermal pad under the die, so the board copper sets the dissipation. With 8 cm² of copper heat sink on the pad the part dissipates 2.5 W in still air; more copper or airflow raises the limit, and 0.3 cm² is the smallest heat-sink area recommended. The package is 1.2 mm high at most.
